page: OVHcloud i1-180 is a storage-optimized server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Haswell processor clocked at 2.2 GHz with no hyperthreading, resulting in 1.0 thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 180.0 GB of system memory, yielding 5.62 GB per core. Storage is a primary feature of this configuration, consisting of 7,650 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network connectivity is supported by an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core capabilities are limited, with the stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core score falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% categories, respectively. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also rank in the bottom 10%. However, the 32 dedicated physical cores compensate in parallel workloads, bringing multi-core benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, into the average tier. Memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks, along with Passmark memory and database operations, consistently registers in the average tier.

The primary tradeoff of the i1-180 is its reliance on older Intel Haswell architecture, which lacks modern instruction sets like AVX-512 or AMX, resulting in weak single-thread execution and lower performance in text processing or LLM text generation. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server delivers high local storage density and dedicated physical cores, making it a viable option for storage-heavy workloads that do not require high single-core compute density. Appropriate workloads include database operations, static web serving, and parallelized data processing tasks that can leverage the 7.6 TB NVMe storage and multi-core architecture.
